newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-IN POSSIBLE LAST GRETZKY-LEMIEUX MEETING, RANGERS BLANK PENS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-IN POSSIBLE LAST GRETZKY-LEMIEUX MEETING, RANGERS BLANK PENS.

text.p: Wayne Gretzky had a goal and an assist in what probably was his final regular-season meeting with Mario Lemieux as the New York Rangers blanked the reeling Pittsburgh Penguins 3-0 Monday.
Gretzky scored into an empty net in the final minute of the third period after setting up the first goal of the game early in the first.
Lemieux, bothered by persistent back pain and still recovering from treatment for Hodgkin's disease, has said this almost certainly will be his final year in the NHL.

"I think it's more the media than anything else," Lemieux said of the hype that preceded the game. "For myself, I just try to enjoy the last few games that I have as much as I can and have some fun with it.
"Obviously, when you're not winning and you're struggling like we are, like I am, it's difficult. You just try to do the best you can with what you've got.
"It is always exciting to play against Wayne," he continued. "To be able to play with him in the Canada Cup and the All-Star Game this year, it is something I enjoyed."
Gretzky also said the publicity leading up to the game got "blown a little out of proportion."
"If Mario had stayed healthy he would have broken my records, especially the one where I got 92 goals in one season," said Gretzky. "He also was capable of getting more than my 162 assists."

Gretzky and Lemieux, the premier players of their era, faced each other 25 times during the regular season. Gretzky's teams went 17-7-1 and he outscored Lemieux in those games, 60 points to 38. Gretzky in 18 seasons has 61 scoring records. Lemieux in 12 seasons has 13 scoring records.
After scoring eight times in five games against New York in last year's playoffs, Lemieux was held without a goal in four regular-season matchups.
"I want to be remembered for coming to the worst team in the NHL and winning two Stanley Cup championships, said Lemieux. "I am at peace with my place in the game's history."
"We have been lucky to have been able to see both Wayne and Mario play," said New York's Mark Messier. "The NHL cannot replace Mario."
Mike Richter recorded his fourth shutout of the season. Richter made 34 saves but was hardly tested en route to his 18th career shutout and first against Pittsburgh.
"Getting a shutout against Mario is special to me," said Richter. "He is so great, a tremendous force one on one."
The Rangers swept the four-game season series, outscoring Pittsburgh 26-8. "We were fortunate (Jaromir) Jagr and (Petr) Nedved weren't playing," said New York coach Colin Campbell.
Bruce Driver and Mike Eastwood also scored for New York, which moved within four points of fourth-place Florida in the Eastern Conference.
The Penguins, 4-16-2 in their last 22 games, fell four points behind the Rangers for fifth place. They also became the last NHL team to be shut out this season.

In Montreal, Jocelyn Thibault came within 2:23 of a shutout and Darcy Tucker and Vincent Damphousse scored 36 seconds apart late in the third period as the Canadiens beat the Boston Bruins 3-1 to move into sole possession of seventh place in the Eastern Conference.
Thibault held the Bruins scoreless until Jozef Stumpel scored during a two-man advantage. He finished with 19 saves.

Martin Rucinksy had a goal and an assist for Montreal, which snapped a six-game home winless streak and improved to 3-1-3 in its last seven games overall. The victory moved the Canadiens past Washington into seventh place in the East, four points ahead of ninth-place Hartford.
In San Jose, Todd Marchant and Ryan Smyth each scored twice and Curtis Joseph made 30 saves as the Edmonton Oilers used a three-goal third period en route to a 5-1 victory over the listless Sharks.

Mariusz Czerkawski also scored and Daniel McGillis had a career-high three assists for Edmonton, which has won three of its last four games. The Oilers, who have taken four of five meetings with the Sharks this season, moved into a fourth-place tie with Phoenix in the Western Conference.
Andrei Nazarov tallied for San Jose, which has lost five straight home games and seven of its last eight overall. The Sharks have a league-low 55 points.

In Vancouver, Vitali Yachmenev scored the tying goal with 3:22 left in the second period and Byron Dafoe made 31 saves as the Los Angeles Kings kept their flickering playoff hopes alive by rallying for a 2-2 tie with the Canucks.

Yachmenev also set up Dimitri Khristich's goal early in the second period for Los Angeles, which is 2-5-2 in its last nine games. The Kings trail Calgary and Chicago by eight points apiece for the final Western Conference playoff spot with eight games remaining.
Lonny Bohonos and Markus Naslund tallied for Vancouver, five points out of the last playoff berth in the West. The Canucks have won just two of their last 12 games (2-7-3).
